## sol-all-diag: a per-node 'may have an attribute' bit in the flat tree (crates/syntax-tree `flat.rs`, builder; crates/syntax `view`)

What: the `FlatTree` builder sets one bit per node when the node has an `ATTR` child, or is the owner of an inner-attribute list (`STMT_LIST` of a fn body, `ITEM_LIST`, `ASSOC_ITEM_LIST`, `MATCH_ARM_LIST`, `EXTERN_ITEM_LIST`, a `SOURCE_FILE`/`BLOCK_EXPR` itself) that has one; false must be certain. Expose it as `Node::may_have_attrs()` (one bit read), and use it in `view::attrs_including_inner` / `HasAttrs::attrs` to return empty at once. A lazy body counts as having one when `block_may_start_with_inner_attr` says it may, so nothing is parsed for it.

Why: blaze-diagnostics' `Walk::add` (`lints/syntax.rs`) calls `on()` (the cfg check) and the attribute-macro probe at each of ~400,000 attribute owners for std, each a scan of its children and its inner list (~40 cycles); nearly all have no attribute. The walk enters an owner before its `ATTR` children, so it can't know in pre-order. With the bit, the walk goes from about 6-9 ms to about 3 ms; `decide`'s level maps and every `attrs()` caller gain the same.
